_note: PLACEHOLDER VALUES. Available water capacity (field capacity minus wilting point) in mm of water per m of root zone. Check every value against its source before use.

sand.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (theta_FC minus theta_WP for sand, 0.05 to 0.11 m3/m3); value is the range midpoint

theta_fc.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (Allen et al. 1998), midpoint of the range for sand: 0.07 to 0.17 m3/m3

theta_wp.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (Allen et al. 1998), midpoint of the range for sand: 0.02 to 0.07 m3/m3

porosity.source: Rawls, Brakensiek and Saxton (1982), Estimation of soil water properties, Trans. ASAE 25(5): 1316-1320, Table 2 total porosity for sand

loam.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (theta_FC minus theta_WP for loam, 0.11 to 0.20 m3/m3); value is the range midpoint

theta_fc.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (Allen et al. 1998), midpoint of the range for loam: 0.2 to 0.3 m3/m3

theta_wp.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (Allen et al. 1998), midpoint of the range for loam: 0.07 to 0.17 m3/m3

porosity.source: Rawls, Brakensiek and Saxton (1982), Estimation of soil water properties, Trans. ASAE 25(5): 1316-1320, Table 2 total porosity for loam

clay.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (theta_FC minus theta_WP for clay, 0.12 to 0.20 m3/m3); value is the range midpoint

theta_fc.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (Allen et al. 1998), midpoint of the range for clay: 0.32 to 0.4 m3/m3

theta_wp.source: FAO-56 Table 19 (Allen et al. 1998), midpoint of the range for clay: 0.2 to 0.24 m3/m3

porosity.source: Rawls, Brakensiek and Saxton (1982), Estimation of soil water properties, Trans. ASAE 25(5): 1316-1320, Table 2 total porosity for clay

_note_soil_water: theta_fc, theta_wp and porosity convert NASA POWER GWETPROF soil wetness (fraction of pore space filled) to volumetric water: theta = GWETPROF x porosity. Starting soil water = TAW x clamp((theta - theta_wp) / (theta_fc - theta_wp), 0, 1).
